newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa rejects fuel-related fares hike.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa rejects fuel-related fares hike.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG said it has no plans to raise passenger fares due to the soaring price of jet fuel.
The market price of jet fuel has risen 30 percent since mid-July, prompting carriers to review costs and prices.
The German national carrier said it did not plan to match price hikes by British Airways, Scandinavian Airline System, American Airlines, Sabena and other European carriers.
BA will raise fares on European routes by 2.5 percent from mid-October, SAS and Sabena will increase by similar amounts on UK flights and American will match the 2.5 percent rise on U.S.-UK routes.
A Lufthansa spokeswoman told Reuters: "The development of different costs is observed very closely but a tariff increase is not a subject for us."
She added: "On the contrary, we want to position ourselves as an attractive (-priced) airline."
Lufthansa had introduced special offers such as its World Discoveries campaign and new autumn savings prices for destinations such as Canada, she pointed out.
